title: Palisades (Holtec restart): External_Sender Palisades Nuclear Power Plant - no Significant Hazards Considerations [['E-Mail']]

documents.text:
From:         Pamela Richard
To:           Marlayna Doell
Subject:      [External_Sender] Pallisades Nuclear Power Plant- No Significant Hazards Considerations
Date:         Thursday, October 8, 2026 2:42:03 PM


My name is Pam Richard and I live on the shore of Lake Michigan in
Milwaukee, WI, vacation in Door County on Lake Michigan

 I have passed Point Beach Power plant many times, just across the water, not
that far from Palisades. Palisades and the Point Beach Unit 2 reactor,
which are the two worst-embrittled RPVs in the country. Watchdogs
have warned about Palisades' embrittlement for more than three
decades. A meltdown would cause: a thousand acute radiation
poisoning deaths; 7,000 radiation injuries; 10,000 latent cancer deaths;
and billions in property damage downwind and downstream.
Neutron-embrittlement of the reactor pressure vessel (RPV), and risk
of through-wall fracture from pressurized thermal shock, are large. No
NRC weakening safety regulations to accommodate continued
operations at age-degraded reactors and endangering our drinking
water and air.

I speak for many of us in Wisconsin, opposing Holtec International's
unprecedented, unwise effort to restart the long closed Palisades
atomic reactor and we object to their refueling plans.


"Viktoria Mitlyng, a senior public affairs officer for the NRC,
confirmed that the fuel assembly tipped and did not drop inside
the reactor vessel. She also said no radioactive materials were
released as a result.

“The incident is under review and the NRC’s conclusions will be
documented in a future inspection report. There has been no
radiological release and no workers or the public have been
affected,” Mitlyng said. ( Sheri McWhirter | smcwhirter@mlive.com )

I am skeptical about this assurance, we've heard this before, and
later it turns out there was harm caused and it indicates that in
the rush to reopen the reactor safety precautions are being
disregarded.

Please protect us from a potential disaster which could affect all
 residents on the shore of Lake Michigan.

Pamela Richard

3302 N Bremen St

Milwaukee, WI 53212
